items.title: Warren Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 23, 1995
items.q: we went up to play the last set, Roy calls a tune, we play the first chorus, and he points at me to take the first solo

ctx.x: He couldn’t resist a challenge I guess.

Well I mean he used to make that, but that was, there’s another thing I’d like to address. I mean Roy was always, always up for a challenge, always would put you in the situation of a challenge. And somehow, when he beat you, you never felt put down, it was an honor. A quick story is one night I think we got done at Condon’s early. It might have been about one o’clock in the morning, and I was across the street getting in my car to go home. And I see Roy coming out of Ryan’s, running across the street. He says,…
That’s great. The stories I’ve read about that kind of thing in Kansas City and that all night jam session. It’s such a great learning experience and I don’t know if it’s still happening these days.
